content.user_title: Moderate Content with Azure AI Safety
content.value_statement: Content moderation is hard to implement consistently across text and images. This skill gives Python examples for Azure AI Content Safety analysis and blocklists.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation of the azure-ai-contentsafety Python package.
Demonstrates API key and Entra ID authentication for ContentSafetyClient.
Explains text analysis for hate, self-harm, sexual, and violence categories.
Shows image analysis from local files and hosted image URLs.
Demonstrates custom text blocklists and halt_on_blocklist_hit behavior.
Summarizes severity levels and eight-level output mode.
limitations: Requires an Azure AI Content Safety resource, endpoint, and valid credentials.
Does not create Azure resources or manage billing.
Does not define your moderation policy or legal obligations.
Examples need application-specific testing before production use.

use_cases.title: Add comment moderation
use_cases.description: Use the text analysis examples to check user comments before publishing.

use_cases.title: Review generated content
use_cases.description: Screen AI-generated text or images before showing them to users.

use_cases.title: Tune blocklist enforcement
use_cases.description: Create custom blocklists for product-specific terms and immediate rejection rules.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a text flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use Azure AI Content Safety in Python to analyze user text for harm categories and severity levels.

prompt_templates.title: Add image moderation
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to analyze a local image and a hosted image with the Azure AI Content Safety Python SDK.

prompt_templates.title: Design blocklist rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create and use a custom text blocklist with halt_on_blocklist_hit for a product moderation workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Build a severity policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me map Azure Content Safety severity levels to allow, review, and block decisions for my application.

output_examples.input: I need to moderate user comments before publishing.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline client setup, text analysis categories, severity checks, and a threshold-based publish decision.

output_examples.input: I want to reject product-specific banned terms immediately.
output_examples.output: The skill would describe creating a text blocklist, adding terms, enabling immediate stopping, and checking blocklist matches.

output_examples.input: I need image moderation for uploaded files.
output_examples.output: The skill would explain reading image bytes, preparing the image for analysis, and reviewing returned category severities.

best_practices: Store Azure credentials in environment variables or managed identity.
Set severity thresholds before using results in production decisions.
Review moderation logs for accuracy while protecting user privacy.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Azure keys in application source files.
Do not treat severity scores as a complete policy decision.
Do not send user content to Azure without required consent and disclosures.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps integrate Azure AI Content Safety moderation into Python applications.

faq.question: Does it support both text and images?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover text analysis, local image analysis, and hosted image analysis.

faq.question: Can it use managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an Entra ID authentication pattern with DefaultAzureCredential.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. You need an existing Azure AI Content Safety resource and credentials.

faq.question: Can I use custom blocklists?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to create blocklists, add items, and stop analysis on a match.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for policy review?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK usage patterns, not legal, safety, or policy approval.
